key_insight: Censored, open-weight LLMs (e.g., models deployed with real-world content restrictions) provide a realistic, natural testbed for studying secret-knowledge elicitation, honesty elicitation, and lie detection—bridging the gap between synthetic lie datasets and real-world model behavior.
problem_solved: Existing evaluations of honesty elicitation and lie detection rely on synthetic or adversarially-trained lie models that may not reflect how models with real censorship or concealment behave; this paper addresses the lack of realistic benchmarks for probing and detecting withheld or false model outputs.
method: Collect and analyze open-weight LLMs that have been censored or restricted in deployment (natural instances of withheld knowledge).
Apply and compare honesty-elicitation techniques (prompt engineering, targeted weight adjustments) to attempt to recover or reveal withheld information.
Train and evaluate lie-detection classifiers on model outputs from these censored LLMs and compare performance to prior synthetic benchmarks.
impact: Provides practitioners with a more realistic evaluation framework for honesty and lie-detection methods, improving trustworthiness assessments and guiding defenses against information withholding in deployed models.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: censored LLM → elicitation methods (prompts/weight changes) → outputs → lie-detection classifier.
Bar chart comparing detection/elicitation success rates on censored models vs. synthetic lie models.
Iconic illustration of 'censorship barrier' between knowledge and output (padlock/filter) to convey natural withholding.
Confusion matrix or ROC curve visualizing classifier performance on real vs. synthetic withheld responses.
paper_title: Censored LLMs as a Natural Testbed for Secret Knowledge Elicitation
paper_authors: Helena Casademunt, Bartosz Cywiński, Khoi Tran, Arya Jakkli, Samuel Marks
